entries.test: Public comparisons of LLM reliability and correctness against well-specified conventional algorithms on the algorithmic tasks discussed would test whether LLMs can substitute for them.
entries.note: Marcus quotes his own earlier conclusion and reaffirms it here.
The substantive assertion concerns a future technological route. Neither 'direct route' nor society-transforming AGI has a sufficiently shared test here.
'Weak sauce' evaluates the replies without specifying factual errors or a standard of adequacy.

entries.test: Published evaluations across successive LLMs would show whether failures recur in planning, reasoning, and generalization.
entries.note: The claim asserts recurring limitations, not universal failure.

entries.test: The Tufts study's VLA success rates across increasing Tower of Hanoi sizes, compared with the Apple study's LLM results, would settle the asserted failure pattern.
entries.note: Read in context, this describes the evaluated models rather than every possible VLA.

entries.test: The Tufts study's success rates for its hybrid and VLA models on unseen Tower of Hanoi variants would settle the generalization comparison.
entries.note: The study and task delimit the comparison.

entries.test: Reported energy measurements for the hybrid and VLAs in the Tufts study would show whether the hybrid's energy use was nearly a hundredfold lower.
Public energy and task-performance comparisons with alternative methods would test LLM efficiency in error-tolerant pattern recognition and in planning.
entries.note: The preceding energy comparison supplies the plain reading of efficiency.

entries.test: Comparing the Tufts methods and results with the Apple paper's findings would show whether they independently corroborate the reported generalization failures.
entries.note: 'Vindicates' has a concrete reading here because Marcus identifies the findings allegedly replicated and extended.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and evaluations of neurosymbolic systems would show whether adopting that approach alone supplies a complete general-purpose solution or leaves substantive capability gaps.
entries.note: The following purpose-built versus general-purpose example gives 'not a panacea' a concrete reading.

entries.test: Public evaluations and reproducible coding examples for the referenced Claude version would show whether it makes recurring errors requiring human verification.
entries.note: The normalization turns 'does seem genuinely impressive to me' into an unqualified judgment. The recurring-error and reliability assertions are testable.

entries.test: Public capability evaluations would show whether the referenced Claude Code system achieves general human-level competence across intellectual tasks beyond coding.
entries.note: The antecedent is Claude Code. General competence supplies a plain reading despite disputed boundaries of AGI.
Marcus offers growing grounds for a possibility, retaining 'reason to think' and 'potential' rather than committing to superior outcomes.
He expresses his preference between hypothetical investments. The normalization strengthens that into a societal obligation concerning its next trillion dollars.
